title: How to take the cough syrup
scenario: Your flatmate Tom has a bad cough and a new bottle of syrup. He does not read English well and does not drive. He asks you to read the leaflet and tell him how to use it.

text: Honey-Lemon Cough Syrup. For adults and children over 6.
Take one spoon (5 ml) three times a day: in the morning, at lunchtime and before bed.
Do not take more than three spoons in one day.
Do not drive if you feel sleepy.
Keep the bottle in a cool place. The syrup contains sugar.
Stop and see a doctor if your cough lasts more than seven days.

task.audience: a flatmate who cannot read the leaflet
task.prompt: Write a message to Tom (35–60 words) with the instructions he needs to take the syrup safely.

points.idea: Three times a day (morning, lunchtime, bed).
Never more than three spoons in a day.
See a doctor if the cough lasts more than seven days.

model: Hi Tom, the leaflet says you take one spoon of the syrup three times a day, morning, lunchtime and bedtime. Never take more than three spoons in a day. If your cough is still there after seven days, please go and see a doctor. Get well soon!
useful: Please go and see a doctor if …
tips: With medicine, numbers are the most important part: how much, how often, the daily maximum. Check each one twice.
Add a clear warning sign ("Never …", "see a doctor if …") so the reader knows what to do if something goes wrong.
explain: Tom must know the dose, the three times, the daily limit and when to see a doctor. Because he does not drive, the sleepiness warning can go; shaking, sugar and storage are small extras.
